official.deadline_central_display: 30 September (the call runs 10 April - 30 September each year)
official.deadline_note: The HFA publishes a single annual application period of 10 April to 30 September. There is no rolling or institutional deadline; the application form is visible only inside that window.
official.application_cycle: Annual: call 10 April - 30 September, application review October - November, results announced in December, accepted exchange periods must start by May of the following year
official.status_note: The HFA publishes the application period as 10 April to 30 September. As of 10 October 2026 that window has closed for this cycle; results are announced in December and the next call is expected in the same April-September window.
official.funding_period: per month, maximum EUR 10,000 per award
benefits: EUR 2,500 per month for the duration of the exchange period, with a maximum of EUR 10,000 according to the length of the project
Grants of up to EUR 10,000 to undertake specialised heart failure research or training in an ESC member country outside your own
Support to participate in or conduct research in a partner laboratory or clinical centre and to study or learn new procedures
Encouragement to submit an abstract to the annual Heart Failure Congress after the project, with the possibility of presenting on the HFA stage with your supervisor
eligibility: Be under 40 years old as of the application deadline
Be an HFA Member, or Fellow of the HFA

Hold an MD but not yet have obtained a post defined as 'permanent', 'senior staff' or 'consultant', and demonstrate expertise in heart failure through examination, practice, scientific publication in a relevant journal or abstract presentation at a national or international meeting; OR
Hold a PhD, DPhil degree or equivalent, or have submitted a thesis before starting the research period relating to the grant
Carry out the project in an ESC member country outside your own country
Prepare the project proposal in collaboration with the proposed host centre for a period of minimum three months
Apply preferably to one of the HFA ICARe-HF Accredited Centres
requirements: Hold HFA membership or Fellowship at the time of application
Prepare the candidate project description jointly with the proposed supervisor
Obtain the completed document from the current head of department or supervisor
Obtain the completed document from the future supervisor
Obtain a letter of recommendation, for example from a head of department or supervisor
Submit through the applications section of your My ESC account
documents: CV covering postgraduate career and present employment, previous training in clinical cardiology, research experience, academic record, and publications in refereed journals with journal titles, page numbers and names of co-authors
Document completed by the current head of department or supervisor
Candidate project description, prepared jointly with the proposed supervisor
Document completed by the future supervisor
Letter of recommendation (for example from the head of department or supervisor)
selection_criteria: Feasibility and importance of the project, with an assessment of sustained benefits for local and global cardiovascular disease reduction - 50%
Candidate's profile: optimal career stage and achievements so far - 20%
Citizenship or permanent residence in a low- or middle-income country as defined by the World Bank - 20%
Quality of the host centre in the research or training field and its track record or expertise in the topic of the application - 10%
coverage: EUR 2,500 per month for the length of the project, capped at EUR 10,000
Funding to carry out research in a partner laboratory or clinical centre and to learn new procedures
application_method: Log in to the applications section of your My ESC account
Click 'New Grant Application' and then 'Apply now' next to the HFA grants programme application form
Complete and upload the CV, the two supervisor documents, the project description and the letter of recommendation before the 30 September deadline
If the form is not visible, check that your My ESC account information is accurate and then contact support under Grants & Fellowships / HFA Research and Training grants
official.application_route: Submit online through the applications section of your My ESC account between 10 April and 30 September; the form appears only inside that window and only if your profile meets the eligibility criteria.
official.study_mode: Research or clinical training placement at a host centre abroad (minimum three months)
official.citizenship_residency: No nationality restriction, but citizenship or permanent residence in a low- or middle-income country as defined by the World Bank carries 20% of the selection score, and the project must be conducted in an ESC member country other than your own
official.international_eligibility: Yes - mobility is mandatory: the host centre must be in an ESC member country outside the applicant's own country
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Heart failure research or clinical training only; the applicant must be an HFA Member or Fellow of the HFA
official.research_requirement: A candidate project description prepared jointly with the proposed supervisor is required, for a project of at least three months
official.duration: Minimum three months; the grant is paid at EUR 2,500 per month up to a maximum of EUR 10,000
official.description: The Heart Failure Association of the European Society of Cardiology gives grants of up to EUR 10,000 so that young members under 40 can carry out specialised heart failure research or training in a partner laboratory or clinical centre in another ESC member country.
official.program_type: Professional association research and training grant with mandatory mobility

applicant_utility.summary: Membership is the gate, not the science: you must already be an HFA Member or Fellow when you apply, so join before September rather than planning to join alongside the application. The scoring is unusually transparent - half the marks sit on the project's feasibility and its sustained benefit for cardiovascular disease reduction, a further 20% on World Bank low- or middle-income country citizenship or residence, and only 10% on the host centre - so a modest centre with a strong heart failure question beats a famous centre with a vague one. Build the file around your supervisor: two of the five required uploads are documents they must complete themselves, and they cannot be chased on the last day.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Cardiologists and heart failure researchers under 40 who already hold HFA membership and want a three-month-plus research or clinical training stint in another ESC country.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your HFA membership or Fellowship is active before the window opens in April
Check your age against the deadline date, not the project start date
Choose an ICARe-HF Accredited Centre if you can, or otherwise a centre with a visible track record in your exact topic
Draft the project description with your future supervisor so the three-month minimum is realistic and the feasibility argument is explicit
Ask your current head of department or supervisor for their document early, since it is a required upload
common_rejection_risks: Applying without active HFA membership or Fellowship, which is a hard eligibility condition
Being 40 or older at the application deadline
A project shorter than the three-month minimum
A vague feasibility or impact argument, which carries half the selection score
Holding a permanent, senior staff or consultant post if you apply on the MD route
Choosing a host centre with no track record in the specific topic of the application
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The page does not state what the EUR 2,500 monthly payment covers or whether travel and relocation are reimbursed, so assume relocation, flights and any institutional fees come from your own funds.
document_audit: The CV must itemise publications in refereed journals with journal titles, page numbers and co-author names - a bare list of papers is not what the form asks for
The project description must be prepared jointly with the proposed supervisor, so allow time for genuine collaboration
Two separate supervisor documents are required: one from your current head of department or supervisor, one from the future supervisor
The application form is only visible during the application period and only if your My ESC profile meets the criteria, so test access in April rather than September
alerts: The form disappears outside 10 April - 30 September, and results only arrive in December
Accepted exchange periods must start by May of the following year, so visa and work-plan arrangements must be ready months after the award
Recipients must submit a report at the end of the project and tell the HFA which appointment they intend to take

Any publication must carry the exact acknowledgement sentence 'The author acknowledges funding received from the Heart Failure Association of the ESC in the form of an HFA Grant', with a print-off sent to the HFA
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: My ESC account, 'New Grant Application', HFA grants programme, with the CV, both supervisor documents, the joint project description and the recommendation letter uploaded before 30 September.
